web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Stock Trades Here — Market Expectations vs. Peers
question: What growth and margin trajectory does Cirrus Logic's current $115.72 share price already assume, and how does its valuation compare against analog and mixed-signal semiconductor peers?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. In a single-customer franchise, the discount is rarely a gift—it is an insurance premium.
epigraph.author: Institutional Equity Desk Maxim (adapted from Warren Buffett)

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Deconstructing Today's Price: The $115.72 Valuation Baseline

web_blocks.html: At the November 24, 2026 close, Cirrus Logic trades at $115.72 per share [27][28]. That sits 35.86% below its 52-week high of $180.42 and 10.10% above its $105.10 low [28]. Basic market cap on 49.86 million shares is $5.77 billion [27]. On 51.48 million diluted shares (Q2 FY2027), diluted equity value is $5,957.27 million [2]. Subtracting $1,076.43 million in cash and marketable securities ($20.91 per share) with zero funded debt leaves a diluted enterprise value (EV) of $4,880.84 million [2]. Finviz prints a $5.15 billion EV because it excludes long-term marketable securities [27].

On headline ratios, CRUS looks cheap next to its own history and analog peers. Shares trade at 14.61x trailing P/E, 14.80x forward P/E, 10.03x EV/EBITDA, 2.51x EV/Sales, and 10.96x P/FCF [27]. Per FullRatio, CRUS averaged 18.21x P/E over 3 years, 18.96x over 5 years, and 20.06x over 10 years [29]. Its decade range spans 11.89x (June 2022) to 33.20x (March 2023) [29]. Today's 14.61x P/E sits 27% below the 10-year norm [29]. Yet on Price-to-Sales, CRUS at 2.82x sits slightly above its 10-year mean of 2.76x (Macrotrends) [27][30]. That gap shows how peak 53.1% gross margins—not depressed sales multiples—drive the low P/E [27].

Why will the market not pay 20x earnings for a debt-free chipmaker with 34.7% operating ROIC? Chapters 4 through 6 give three clear reasons. First, Apple rose to 91% of sales in FY2026 and 93% in Q2 FY2027 [1][2]. No buyback can remove that binary customer risk. Second, Q3 FY2027 sales guidance ($510M–$570M; $540M midpoint) implies a 7% YoY drop and missed the $563.5M consensus [3][31]. Consensus models -15.47% EPS contraction this year and -0.14% next year [27]. Third, the 10-year Treasury yields 4.92% (as of November 23, 2026), raising the hurdle rate for slow-growth hardware [32].

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Reverse DCF & 10-Year Ex-SBC Free Cash Flow Valuation

web_blocks.html: We anchor fair value on normalized ex-SBC owner free cash flow, not FY2026's flattered headline cash flow. FY2026 produced $650.60 million in CFO and $636.61 million in FCF [1]. Roughly $102 million of that inflow came from a one-time working-capital and prepaid-wafer release [1]. Normalizing CFO to $548.6 million, deducting ~$37 million for steady-state capex and H1 FY2027 R&D step-up, and subtracting $81.81 million of FY2026 stock-based compensation (4.1% of sales) [1] leaves a clean $430.0 million ex-SBC FCF base (FCF0).

Using a 4.92% 10-year Treasury yield [32], a 1.17 beta [27], and a 5.0% equity risk premium gives a 10.77% CAPM cost of equity. With zero debt, we round Base WACC to 10.8% (11.5% Bear; 10.5% Bull). At 10.8% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth, today's $115.72 price ($4,880.8M EV) implies roughly +1.2% annual ex-SBC FCF growth (+1.5% yields $117.06). In plain terms, the market prices CRUS as a 1%–2% real-growth cash cow with a permanent Apple discount.

web_blocks.takeaway: At $115.72, CRUS sits just 8.9% below our $126.00 ex-SBC Base value ($126.25 exact). Net cash ($20.91/sh) cushions Bear downside near $84.50, but Base upside is too thin for a 1.50:1 risk-reward setup.

web_blocks.title: 7.3 Quantitative Peer Benchmarking: Analog & Mixed-Signal Semiconductor Comps

web_blocks.html: We benchmark CRUS against six analog and mobile chip peers: TXN, ADI, MPWR, SLAB, QCOM, and STM [27][33][34][35][36][37][38]. Broad analog leaders TXN, ADI, and MPWR earn 20x–49x EV/EBITDA because they serve diverse industrial, auto, and data-center buyers with 20%–40% sales growth [33][34][35]. Mobile-heavy peers QCOM (13.65x forward P/E) and CRUS (14.80x forward P/E) remain stuck in a 13x–15x band [27][37]. Even after November 24's sharp analog sell-off (TXN -11.25%, ADI -17.37%, MPWR -10.77%, STM -8.71%), CRUS's 10.03x EV/EBITDA reflects concentration and low growth—not neglect.

web_blocks.takeaway: CRUS posts 53.1% gross margin and 18.0% ROIC at the group's lowest EV/EBITDA (10.03x), yet 5.1% sales growth and 93% Apple share tether its multiple to QCOM rather than TXN, ADI, or MPWR.

web_blocks.region_era: United States, 2021–2026 Mobile RF Supercycle & Concentration De-Rating
web_blocks.mechanism: Skyworks posted 50%+ gross margins, high cash conversion, and steady buybacks while deriving 65%–70% of sales from Apple RF modules. Once smartphone volumes stalled and Apple built in-house cellular silicon, Wall Street compressed Skyworks' multiple years before full socket losses hit.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: SWKS compressed from ~22x P/E and ~$200/share in 2021 to ~$77/share (~11x–13x earnings) by November 2026—a >60% drop despite staying profitable throughout [39].
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Low trailing multiples (10x EV/EBITDA, 14.6x P/E) do not stop multi-year dead-money outcomes when one buyer exceeds 70%–90% of sales. Re-rating requires real non-Apple growth, not buybacks alone.

web_blocks.title: 7.4 Wall Street Consensus vs. Our Independent Valuation

web_blocks.html: Sell-side analysts stay mildly upbeat, with Finviz and Zacks showing a $136.67 mean target (+18.1%) and MarketBeat citing $147.50–$160.00 after the November 4 EPS beat ($2.70 vs. $2.42) [27][31][40]. Our $126.00 Base value sits $10.67 lower for two clear reasons. First, sell-side models capitalize non-GAAP EPS (ignoring $81.81M of annual SBC), while we deduct SBC as real cash. Second, consensus assigns zero odds to Apple socket erosion or further 2027 PC delays. At $115.72, CRUS is fairly priced.

Valuation Upgrade Trigger: Either a washout below $100.00 (creating >=26% upside to $126.00 Base value) or verifiable non-Apple growth >15% of revenue that lifts normalized ex-SBC FCF growth above 6%.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I turn to the market tape and ask the single most important question in investing: what is Mr. Market actually charging us for Cirrus Logic today, and why? At the November 24, 2026 close, CRUS changes hands at $115.72 per share. That is 35.86% below its 52-week high of $180.42 and barely 10.1% above its 52-week low of $105.10. On a diluted share count of 51.48 million, you are looking at a $5.96 billion equity market cap. Subtract the $1.08 billion cash fortress sitting on the balance sheet with zero funded debt, and the entire operating business—all 4,340 patents, the 22-nanometer custom audio codecs, the boosted amplifiers, the camera controllers, and the emerging PC SoundWire franchise—is being priced at an enterprise value of $4.88 billion.

At first glance, any value investor's pulse quickens. You are looking at 14.61x trailing GAAP earnings, 14.80x forward earnings, 10.03x EV/EBITDA, and 10.96x trailing free cash flow. Over the last decade, Cirrus Logic averaged a 20.06x P/E multiple; over the last five years, it averaged 18.96x. Today's 14.61x multiple sits 27% below its ten-year norm. So let us pause and ask the skeptical question every seasoned analyst must ask before reaching for the buy button: is the market being foolish, or is the market charging a rational insurance premium?

When we put our price-blind forensic audit from Chapters 1 through 6 alongside that 14.61x multiple, the market's skepticism snaps into sharp focus. First, Apple concentration did not shrink over the past five years—it climbed from 79% in FY2017 to 91% in FY2026 and hit an eye-watering 93% in Q2 FY2027. Second, management just guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to $510 million–$570 million, a 7% year-over-year decline at the midpoint that fell short of Wall Street's $563.5 million estimate. Third, the risk-free 10-year U.S. Treasury yield sits at 4.92%, lifting Cirrus Logic's CAPM cost of equity to 10.8%. When a business grows revenue at 2.9% annually over nine years and depends on one customer for 93 cents of every dollar, a 14.6x multiple is not an anomaly—it is equilibrium.

Let us test that intuition with clean, unvarnished cash-flow arithmetic. In FY2026, Cirrus Logic printed $636.61 million in headline free cash flow, which looks extraordinary until you notice that roughly $102 million came from a one-time working-capital and prepaid-wafer inventory release. Strip out that non-recurring release, normalize capital expenditures and the H1 FY2027 R&D step-up from the INVENTVM acquisition, and—crucially—deduct $81.81 million of annual stock-based compensation as a genuine cash cost to owners. You arrive at a true, steady-state ex-SBC owner free cash flow baseline of $430 million.

Now plug $430 million into a 10-year discounted cash flow model at a 10.8% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth. What growth rate does today's $115.72 price already assume? Roughly 1.2% to 1.5% annual free cash flow growth for the next decade. Think about that. If Cirrus Logic executes modestly—growing ex-SBC free cash flow at 3.0% for five years and 2.5% thereafter as HPMS content offsets flat iPhone units—our exact Base fair value lands at $126.00 per share ($126.25 unrounded). That is only 8.9% above today's $115.72 price. In a Bull case where Windows AI PC SoundWire adoption and HPMS power/camera wins accelerate FCF growth to 7% for five years, fair value reaches $160.50 (+38.7%). In a Bear case where Apple squeezes margins or re-architects a major socket (-5% annual FCF decline for five years at an 11.5% WACC), the $20.91 per share of net cash cushions equity value near $84.50 (-27.0%).

Compare Cirrus Logic against its semiconductor neighborhood and the structural valuation gap becomes unmistakable. Diversified analog giants like Texas Instruments (22.4x EV/EBITDA), Analog Devices (20.0x EV/EBITDA), and Monolithic Power Systems (48.8x EV/EBITDA) trade at double to quadruple Cirrus Logic's multiple because their revenue spans tens of thousands of industrial, automotive, and AI data-center sockets. Meanwhile, mobile-concentrated Qualcomm trades at 13.65x forward earnings—almost identical to CRUS's 14.80x. And remember Skyworks Solutions: another high-margin, cash-rich Apple supplier that de-rated from 22x earnings and $200/share in 2021 to ~$77/share by 2026 as smartphone volumes matured and customer in-housing fears capped its multiple. Cheap trailing ratios cannot force a re-rating on their own; only verifiable, non-Apple growth can.

Let us pause and examine one subtle valuation trap that trips up even experienced institutional analysts when they study fabless semiconductor companies: the gap between GAAP earnings, non-GAAP earnings, and true owner free cash flow. Wall Street's $136.67 mean price target—and bullish targets up to $160—almost always anchor on non-GAAP earnings per share, which conveniently add back $81.81 million of annual stock-based compensation as if issuing equity to Austin and Edinburgh mixed-signal engineers costs shareholders nothing. When you run a semiconductor R&D lab with 1,815 employees competing directly against Apple, Qualcomm, and Texas Instruments for analog design talent, stock-based compensation is not a one-time accounting quirk; it is permanent payroll. Cirrus Logic's management deserves genuine credit for retiring far more shares than it issues—spending $279.96 million on buybacks in FY2026 against $81.81 million of SBC—yet every dollar spent merely neutralizing dilution is a dollar that cannot compound intrinsic value per share.

Sensitivity analysis confirms how tightly Cirrus Logic's valuation is hemmed in by today's interest-rate regime. With the 10-year U.S. Treasury yielding 4.92%, every 50-basis-point increase in our discount rate trims roughly $5.50 per share off Base intrinsic value. Conversely, even if you stretch our Base growth rate from 3.0% to 4.0% over the next five years, fair value climbs only to about $130 per share—still leaving just 12% upside against a 27% Bear downside. In other words, you do not need to be a raging bear to conclude that CRUS lacks a margin of safety at $115.72; you simply have to respect the arithmetic of high risk-free rates and single-customer risk.

book_callouts.title: Narrator's Reflection: The Value-Trap Optical Illusion
book_callouts.text: When you see a debt-free chipmaker trading at 10x EV/EBITDA with 53% gross margins, every instinct whispers 'bargain.' Resist that shortcut. Once you strip out FY2026's one-time $102M working-capital tailwind and treat $81.8M of annual stock-based compensation as real cash, CRUS's Base intrinsic value is $126.00—less than 9% above today's price. In a world where 10-year Treasuries pay nearly 5% risk-free, an 8.9% margin of safety is nowhere near enough compensation for 93% single-customer concentration.
